dialog: We'll have to leave these lands unless it changes...

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: We're searching for missing people, namely my husband. Would you have any knowledge about that?

speaker: Sebastian
dialog: I'm afraid not my lady, but it would be safe to assume the cases are linked.

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: Yes it would. Master Awotruce, we would like to accept Master Sebastian under our wing, and away from your jaws if that's acceptable with you.

speaker: Narrator
dialog: The direwolf nods.

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: We humbly accept your benevolence, Master Awotruce. It would seem our lead is the Temple. Let us be on our way.

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: We humbly accept your benevolence, Master Awotruce. It would seem our lead is the Temple.

speaker: Hogmother
dialog:
Those woods sure look bad........
Oh Hogfather where did you get yourself into...

speaker: Amyssa
dialog: Excuse me, Madam Hogmother

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: Yes dear? Is something wrong?

speaker: Amyssa
dialog: I'm curious, since you're a Shaman, what is it like, seeing the spirits world?

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: Well here in the material plane you can either have a big object or shatter it, where for spirits they wouldn't see much difference.

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: Things that are whole or completely warped and broken are still just receptacle for spirits, and its integrity doesn't matter to them.

speaker: Amyssa
dialog: And the sights, and scenery, are they not different?

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: Oh it's a lot like this world, except the roads aren't as straight as they are here, they are winding and twisting, and they go forth and back at the same time.

speaker: Amyssa
dialog: Oh, how is that?

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: Because the living think they're making their own path when it's been set by destiny long before them.

speaker: Amyssa
dialog: Oh, but what if they don't go in their path?

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: Oh, you'd shouldn't talk about that, better just find your destiny and pursue it.

speaker: Amyssa
dialog: But what if they're wrong?

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: They can't be, all the ways will lead them there, it's just a matter, of how many accidents and how much suffering they're willing to endure before adjusting their path.

speaker: Amyssa
dialog: And what if they die before they reach it?

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: Oh, that's just one step in the journey for the spirit, they keep going until their destiny is reached.

speaker: Amyssa
dialog: And what happens then? Do they finally die too?

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: That I do not know.

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: There's seems to be a clearing up ahead.

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: This must be the forest glade.

speaker: Narrator
dialog: The party reaches a central raisen location in the woods, they can  overlook the different paths from here

speaker: Narrator
dialog: While resting and recuperating from the journey, a figure shows up to the party.

speaker: Trollkin
dialog:
Hello, visitors to the Dark Woods!

I am Trollkin the Trollkin

Nice Trollkin to you! Haaaaaaaa hehehehe.

speaker: Trollkin
dialog: I am da King of this place, and my palace is right by there near the swamp. I am looking for a queen to come live with me.

speaker: Trollkin
dialog: I couldn't help but listening to your conversation about the spirits world. My ancestors comes from a long line of spiritual folks

speaker: Trollkin
dialog: I want you to come be my queen, lady Amyssa.

speaker: Amyssa
dialog:
What?! . . . . How do you know my name?! . . . . 
How did you eavesdropped on our conversation?

speaker: Trollkin
dialog: This is my kingdom your highness, you are just a visitor here. For now!

speaker: Amyssa
dialog: You trollkin truly are vile. Don't you dare come near me

speaker: Amyssa
dialog: I would burn you with my fire darts before you can even spell 'hello'

speaker: Trollkin
dialog: You don't know any fire spells

speaker: Amyssa
dialog: How would you know what are the spells I master?

speaker: Trollkin
dialog: Because I have your spellbook.

speaker: Amyssa
dialog: It's true my spellbook has gone missing!

speaker: Amyssa
dialog: You monster! You've pickpocket me! Bring it back this instance!

speaker: Trollkin
dialog: Oh... so now you'll have dealings with me?

speaker: Trollkin
dialog: Well... you know what I want!! Come to my hut by the swamp later...

speaker: Trollkin
dialog:
HEH.. HEH.. HEH.. HEH.. 

*the trollkin is turning transparent...*

speaker: Trollkin
dialog:
'SEE' YA!!! 

HAAAAAAAAAAAA hahahahaha

speaker: Narrator
dialog: The Trollkin vanishes from sight...

speaker: Amyssa
dialog: NO TROLL!! I WILL BURN YOUR ENTIRE FOREST DOWN!! DO YOU HEAR ME !!!!!

speaker: Amyssa
dialog: I WILL HAVE YOUR SWAMP DREDGED DRY AND YOUR SKIN FLAYED ALIVE !!!!

speaker: Narrator
dialog: Amyssa's voice is thoundering through the woods, but there's no answer...

speaker: Bragain
dialog: Oh, remind me to never piss you off Amyssa.

speaker: Amyssa
dialog:
Oh do shut up. How did I ever get involved with this villain.

Now my spellbook is gone and I'm so far from home...

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: There there my girl. This forest is home to the goddess Narlia.

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: She will never have such crimes committed freely on her blessed grounds.

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: Come, let us go to the shrine, we'll pray to her and await answers.

speaker: Amyssa
dialog: But it's the opposite way from where Hogfather is?

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: Hogfather would have none of that if he knew. It's alright child. We won't find Hogfather but that's where we'll find some peace.

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: There's the shrine. Let's clean it up a bit. I wish I had more to offer as tribute to the goddess.

speaker: Narrator
dialog: The stone shrine is open on all ways. In the center, a risen stone platform marks a spot of sanctity. It is believed that ancient times a divine influnce has poured into the material place through here, and the connection has never severed.

options.text: Make plans to submit Amyssa to the Trollkin
options.frustration_text: You wouldn't be able to do that while Hogmother is in the party.

speaker: Amyssa
dialog: Oh goddess Narlia, how did I get involved in a mess like this. I want to go home.

speaker: Amyssa
dialog: This spellbook cost me a fortune and it's a lot of time to make and write.

speaker: Amyssa
dialog: I'll have to quit the adventure if I am to write a new one, and to cover the costs it's going to take a long time as well.

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: We'll go and attempt to reason with the Trollkin first. We'll see if he can be persuaded.

speaker: Amyssa
dialog: I really doubt a type like his can be. Maybe I'll just offer myself to him and get it over with quickly.

speaker: Amyssa
dialog: I really doubt a type like his can be. Maybe I'll just offer myself to him and get it over with quickly.

options.text: In her [Desperation] Amyssa will go see the Trollkin
Wait for answers from the altar
options.frustration_text: The stone remains cold and still.

speaker: Amyssa
dialog:
I can't believe that beast is waiting there waiting for me to be offered to him.

How will I ever get out of this predicament.

speaker: Claudio
dialog: We can exchange our outfits and I'll seduce the Trollkin.

speaker: Claudio
dialog: I'll put on the performence of my life, while you figure out where the spellbook is kept.

speaker: Claudio
dialog: Bragain you could steal the spellbook back.

speaker: Bragain
dialog: That's a plan to make, but alas I'm not that kind of rogue. There's hardly any stealth in me, and my thieving is underclassed.

speaker: Sebastian
dialog: I will do it.

speaker: Sebastian
dialog: I'm hard to notice, and sneaky as it's possible to be.

speaker: Sebastian
dialog: If you can buy me the time and keep the fiend busy, I'll slip in and look for the Spellbook in their possesion.

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: May Narlia watch over us. This is going to be very dangerous. This Trollkin is a fierce enemy. Prepare well, my dear friends.

speaker: Narrator
dialog: The party will settle for preparations and prayer.

speaker: Claudio
dialog: Well... Whadaya think?

speaker: Amyssa
dialog:
By the goddess!!!

You look amazing Claudio!

speaker: Amyssa
dialog: What a way to steal the show.

speaker: Claudio
dialog: Hehehe, I was born for the stage, and for my crowd. Let us pray this works.

speaker: Amyssa
dialog: Are you sure you're ready to go through with this plan Sebastian? This is going to be very dangerous.

speaker: Amyssa
dialog: I'm so sorry I'm putting you all through this risk, for a minor thing like a Spellbook. Ugh, I hate it!

speaker: Sebastian
dialog: I would gladly stay in my garden if it was possible. I was appointed by our elders, they warned me there will be times like this.

speaker: Sebastian
dialog: If we won't find a way to challenge them directly, it'll spread to every home and every family. It's not just you Amyssa.

speaker: Sebastian
dialog: If we give this villain any ground, the darkness will only spread, it'll never stop taking.

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: Let us swear an auth, upon this altar. If anything goes wrong, we'll never abandon Sebastian, or Claudio, or Amyssa.

speaker: Narrator
dialog: The party finishes their planing and heads out towards that dreaded swamp.

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: Excuse us Master Awotruce. We've returned seeking council.

speaker: Awotruce
dialog: This trollkin is a vile aberration upon my woods. Do not mistaken him for a mere court Jester, He is a dangerous spellcaster and not to be taken lightly.

speaker: Awotruce
dialog: I would gladly maul his throat, but he rarely leaves his swamp, and it's very difficult to track him on ground.

speaker: Awotruce
dialog: I will not take on the swamp, it's too difficult for me to move on.

speaker: Awotruce
dialog: That foe is beyond either of us.

speaker: Awotruce
dialog: I smelt him. The forest says he's harmless.

speaker: Awotruce
dialog: Ah, so it is the Ugress... Cleverly, she never entered my woods, she doesn't leave the fortress and stay behind the walls.

speaker: Awotruce
dialog: It would bring me great honor to tear her to shreds and maul her beyond recognition.

speaker: Awotruce
dialog: If you can make way through the barricades and her armed troops, I will end her on the spot.

speaker: Narrator
dialog: The party anxiously makes its way to the swamp. Moving slowly and surely, looking for signs of an invisible stalker in their midst...

speaker: Claudio
dialog: Okey-Dokey, it's showtime! Oh goddess please watch over me!

speaker: Claudio
dialog: I am absolutely stage-terrified! I've never had such a hostile crowd! And such a dangerous stage!

speaker: Claudio
dialog: I WILL GO FORTH

speaker: Amyssa
dialog: Alright, we'll ambush the creature back here, Sebastian will lurk and head for the back when the fiend is occupied.

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: If anything goes sour, we'll all jump and overwhelm the fiend. All for one and one for all.

speaker: Amyssa
dialog: Wow Claudio, that's some *REAL* good disguise!

speaker: Claudio
dialog:
YOOO HOOO !!

Trollkin..........
Where arrrrrreeeeee youuuuu.......

speaker: Narrator
dialog: The long narrow figure from the swamp makes his way weaving like snake over the risen logs buried into the swamp.

speaker: Narrator
dialog: Right as he goes on shore, the halfling sneaks right behind him silent and unnoticed, and walks through the swamp in a careful motion.

speaker: Trollkin
dialog: HAAAAAAAAAAAA I knew you'd come see me, my pet!

speaker: Trollkin
dialog:
None can resist the mojo of Trollkin!

Come let me show you around your new kingdom.

speaker: Claudio
dialog: Oh you devil you!! I'm not that kind of girl! You'll have put some more effort into me first!

speaker: Claudio
dialog: *Does some tempting flirting and runs off*

speaker: Trollkin
dialog:
HO HO HO HO HO HO HO

HAAAAAAAAAA HAHAHAHA......

speaker: Trollkin
dialog:
YEESSSS!!!!!

I'm gonna get you like a lion prouncing over a gazelle.. Don't you run from me!

speaker: Narrator
dialog: The fiend plays the game of chase with Claudio who keeps his distance while giggling and pretending to play along...

speaker: Narrator
dialog: It is not too long before a signal sparks from the swamp.

speaker: Narrator
dialog: From here it seems like smoke, and a fire has started deeper into the swamp.

speaker: Trollkin
dialog:
Ooooooooh..... what is that???

Did I forget the kettle on?

speaker: Narrator
dialog: As the fiend is retreating back to his hut, the halfling appears and has returned.

speaker: Sebastian
dialog:
I have it.

It was right there laying in his hut. I sparked his nasty straw to mask our exit.

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: Brilliant work Sebastian. Let us retreat, quickly.

speaker: Narrator
dialog: The party rallies with Claudio and hurries away from the swamp...

speaker: Claudio
dialog: Well... how did I do?

speaker: Amyssa
dialog: Oh you've been fantastic!!! And Sebastian went and got the Spellbook back, and distracted the Trollkin!

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: You've been wonderful Claudio, your preformance would please the goddess greatly. Now quick, let's head to the fortress before the Trollkin comes looking for us.

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: Those woods are full with unrest. We're so close now, only those walls stand between me and Hogfather. I wish I didn't have to bring you all through this, but here we are.

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: This should be a good place to signal to our contact.

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: This should be a good place to signal to our contact.

speaker: Narrator
dialog: The Glade in the center of the woods would be the best place for a meetup... it is known to all the inhabitants.

speaker: Narrator
dialog: Like fate, coincidence or plan... the contact does appear in the glade.

speaker: Lurch
dialog: It is I Lurch, I bring you news from within the fortress as agreed upon.

speaker: Lurch
dialog:
The Ugress Hag has taken hold of this area, she has gone completely power mad.
Her motives are kept hidden, but the fiends surrounding her tell no lies.

speaker: Lurch
dialog:
They have began a full military scale industry to outfit their troops.
There are normal folks amongst them brought to provide sustenance.

speaker: Lurch
dialog:
It appear they came by their free will, or perhaps forced by the Ugress Geas.
I will avoid the Ugress if I were you. There is a service tunnel leading downstream towards the Swamp.

speaker: Lurch
dialog: It would be be wise to enter through there, slip in, get your friend and leave. but you would have to be avoiding the Trollkin which dwells nearby.

speaker: Lurch
dialog: Oh, and before you ask, I've met him. I'll have nothing to do with him.

speaker: Lurch
dialog: I'll be awaiting your signal and lead you inside, in secret.
